title: Introduction to Functions
learning_outcomes: Explain what introduction to functions contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: purpose of functions.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Functions package behavior behind named inputs and return values. Clear parameter and return types, small responsibilities, and controlled side effects make code easier to reuse and test. In this lesson, focus on purpose of functions; then compare it with function declarations. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use introduction to functions when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Functions package behavior behind named inputs and return values. Clear parameter and return types, small responsibilities, and controlled side effects make code easier to reuse and test. For introduction to functions, begin with purpose of functions. Also distinguish function declarations; calling functions; function naming conventions. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Introduction to Functions
content_blocks.code:
<?php
function subtotal(int $price, int $quantity): int { return $price * $quantity; }
echo subtotal(6, 4) . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for introduction to functions from top to bottom. Start by identifying purpose of functions, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
